about.title: Dos Palos Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Dos Palos is a small city, but the crash reports still add up on roads like Rt 33, Frank Avenue, Elgin Avenue, and SR-33. Recent county data shows several injury collisions a year here, with Monday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. showing up often in the reports. After a collision, the hours and days that follow matter — insurance adjusters may call quickly, and what you say to them can affect your claim later. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge you anything; we simply connect you with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with Merced County claims. They can help you understand what evidence to preserve, how California's comparative fault rules might apply to your situation, and what your options look like going forward. There's no obligation to move forward after you talk to someone, and no cost to you unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a public road agency — is involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage of blame is assigned to you. Anything you say to the other driver's insurer, including a recorded statement, can be used to shift more fault onto you.

items.title: No Cost Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you receive a settlement or award. That means getting informed about your rights after a Dos Palos crash costs you nothing upfront.

items.question: Do I have to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: No, you're not required to give a recorded statement to the other side's insurer, and it's often better not to before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can minimize what they owe, and early statements can be used against you later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash on Rt 33 or SR-33 in Dos Palos?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government entity, like Caltrans or a local road authority, may be responsible for road conditions, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth getting a claim reviewed quickly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you were partially responsible, though your recovery amount may be reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help assess how fault might be allocated in your specific situation based on the evidence available.
